paras: The killing of Walter Tucker was the fatal shooting of a 27-year-old Black man by Marshal James Walker of Brownsville, apparently in Tennessee, on August 23, 1915. Walker shot Tucker while trying to arrest him, and the only report found gives the officer's account that Tucker resisted.
Tucker was described as "the negro" who had "recently returned from the penitentiary"; the report does not say why he was being arrested.
According to the report, Tucker "refused to be arrested, and started toward the officer when the fatal shot was fired." Marshal Walker's shot killed him.
No report of an inquest, an arrest of the marshal, or any other official action appears in the coverage.

The killing appeared as a brief Brownsville item in the state-news column of the Fayette Falcon of Somerville, Tennessee, on August 27, 1915, under the headline "Officer Kills Negro." The item stated the resisting-arrest version as fact, without naming a source, and ended with a note on Tucker's prison record. No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have carried the story.
